findings.summary: The production spawn cannot launch any worker under the configuration this package itself ships. runChannelWrite injects spawnWorkerProcess({cmd: defaultWorkerCmd(), args: [role, clueId, runId]}) and defaultWorkerCmd() falls back to `bash` when TICK_WORKER_CMD is unset — and nothing in the repo ever sets it: bin/deep-research-loop.sh exports only TICK_ENTRY / TICK_CHANNEL / TRIGGER_STORE_DIR / DD_CLAIM_STALE_MS, and bin/tick-entry.sh sets nothing. So the deployed loop executes `bash dr-worker-code-local <clueId> <runId>`, i.e. bash opening a script path that exists nowhere (no dr-worker-* file exists in the repo; README lists agent-runtime / subagent-mcp as the worker dispatch mechanism), which exits 127 immediately. Spec §1.2's spawn deliverable and §7's premise that a real-machine spawn produces a worker that posts results (and gets 422) are therefore not met: the mapped R1a role is merely an argv token handed to an interpreter. Because §1.3 makes this path live (TICK_CHANNEL defaults to research:p02-smoke-1dce60), every tick CASes open→in_flight, starts nothing, and the next tick reclaims to open — permanent irreversible churn on an append-only bus with zero research progress. The composed default is also never exercised: the wiring test injects spawnWorker (test/tick-run.test.ts:657,685-688) and the primitive test supplies an explicit cmd: process.execPath (test/tick-run.test.ts:712-716), so the launcher and the wiring are verified separately and never together — exactly the split-verification pattern spec §0 and §4.1 disciplines 7/8 forbid.

spawnWorkerProcess resolves on the child's `spawn` event only, so a command that launches and dies immediately (the shipped default `bash <role>` exiting 127) is recorded as spawned: true, the card keeps its in_flight status and run_id, and the S2/N5 compensation (CAS back to open) never fires. Combined with the finding above, `spawned: true` in the --run output is not evidence that any worker started, and the only observable difference between a working launcher and a launcher that does nothing is invisible to both the CLI output and the test suite.

The N13 real-machine evidence overstates what happened. The dev-note reports the dispatch as 'spawn 启动 worker 子进程（spawnWorkerProcess），带 role=dr-worker-code-local、runId=33793a1b…'. With TICK_WORKER_CMD unset — and nothing in the repo exports it — that launch was `bash dr-worker-code-local msg_01KZ6AF6P3SN4B43BYHQAJ8TTW 33793a1b-…`, which cannot start any worker. The note's own follow-up (lines 153-158: the next --run reclaims the card back to open because no started event ever appeared) is the observable confirmation that no worker ran. So the package's N3/N13 real-machine claim ('CAS + spawn 被调用' with a real worker) is not supported by the cited evidence.

The N7 'rationale on the card' fix is asserted only at the decision layer (test/tick.test.ts:314-326 checks decideTick's block decision). The production write path — runWrite's block branch passing decision.rationale into realCas (src/tick-run.ts:233) and realCas merging it into the published payload (src/tick-run.ts:305) — has no publish-body assertion, even though the analogous run_id requirement does have one (the M7 realCas publish-body test). A mutation deleting `if (input.rationale !== undefined) update.rationale = input.rationale;` would leave every test green while blocked cards ship with no rationale.
